title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting: K is an algebraically closed field isomorphic to C, with no isomorphism chosen ('isom non choisi!'). Grothendieck postulates a multiplicative (tensor) functor ξ = ξ_K from motives over K to Z-modules. This is an integral 'Betti' fibre functor, with comparison isomorphisms α_ℓ: ξ⊗_Z Z_ℓ ≅ ξ_ℓ (ℓ-adic realization) and α_∞: ξ⊗_Z K ≅ ξ_K (de Rham realization, K-valued). He then tests what is canonical by looking at the Tate motive: ξ(H^2(P^1, Z(0))) = ξ(Z(-1)) is free of rank 1 over Z, but with no preferred generator. Choosing a generator amounts to orienting P^1_K, viewed as a real 2-manifold (≅ S^2). Equivalently it amounts to choosing one of the two complex structures on P^1_K induced by an isomorphism K ≅ C, i.e. choosing a square root of -1 in K. The page breaks off at 'Comme π ∈ R ⊂ K est bien déterminé…'. The point being set up is that π is canonical, so the de Rham comparison sends a generator of ξ(Z(1)) to ±2πi, and the sign is tied to the choice of i. In modern terms: Z(1)_B = 2πi·Z ⊂ C, which is canonical up to the sign fixed by the orientation (i.e. by the choice of i); the period of the Tate motive is 2πi. The page serves the larger aim of making the Betti fibre functor and the period comparison as intrinsic as possible over a field merely isomorphic to C, presumably on the way to the motivic Galois group, its torsors and periods. Note: the neighbouring pages are Bourbaki 'Systèmes de racines' redaction notes (Tribu 59) and are unrelated; this looks like reuse of scrap paper.
errors: For an abstract field K ≅ C with no isomorphism chosen, P^1_K is not 'naturally' a real manifold. Different isomorphisms K ≅ C (via wild automorphisms of C) induce different topologies, and the subfield R ⊂ K is not determined by the field structure alone. The claims hold only if K is taken as a topological field isomorphic to C, or if the isomorphism is fixed up to complex conjugation. Only then is the ambiguity reduced to Z/2 = {i, -i}, and only then is 'π ∈ R ⊂ K bien déterminé'. Likewise an intrinsic Z-valued Betti functor ξ_K does not exist for an abstract K; it depends on the embedding up to conjugation.

ideas.what: Integral Betti fibre functor on motives over K ≅ C, with comparison isomorphisms to ℓ-adic and de Rham realizations
ideas.modern_name: Betti realization with comparison isomorphisms (realization systems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motive philosophy); formalized by Deligne (Hodge II; Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih LNM 900, 1982), Jannsen
ideas.where_published: Ideas sketched in letters and Récoltes et Semailles; formalized in Saavedra Rivano's thesis (Catégories tannakiennes, LNM 265) and Deligne's work

ideas.what: The Betti realization of Z(1) is canonical only up to sign; a generator corresponds to an orientation of P^1 and hence to a choice of i, with the de Rham comparison giving the period ±2πi
ideas.modern_name: Z(1) = 2πiZ ⊂ C; orientation convention for the Tate twist; period of the Tate motive
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971; 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales', 1979)
ideas.where_published: Standard in Deligne's papers and in SGA 4½ conventions

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard observation that the Betti Tate twist is canonical only up to sign, with sign tied to the choice of √-1 and the period 2πi. It became standard through Deligne. The use of Z-coefficient motives is mildly notable as a document of Grothendieck's thinking, but it contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: '{+mult.+}' is an interlinear insertion 'mult.' above 'foncteur', i.e. 'le foncteur mult[iplicatif]'.
In 'variété [-analytique-] réelle' the word 'analytique' is struck out, so the reading is 'variété réelle'.
The last line reads 'Comme π ∈ R ⊂ K est bien déterminé comme…', with blackboard R (ℝ ⊂ K) and the sentence unfinished.
